CRR retrodiction battery — outcomes
Independent run per the retrodiction prompt. One script (crr_retrodictions.py), no free parameters, every number printed by the
script. Systems chosen per class by the runner; grades per the five-verdict scheme. Cross-listed rows (a system that answers in
two classes) are counted once.

Reading
Where the framework is sharp: on families whose Fisher geometry is the physics' own. Every two-state occupancy law tested
(half-life, logistic inflection, KM/Hill, pKa, Fermi level, Langmuir, laser threshold) is the single statement 'the cut is at occupation
one-half', forced by the Bernoulli family's half-turn with nothing supplied from outside. In quantum dynamics the cut rule
reproduces the Mandelstam–Tamm speed limit and gives the actual cut time for spin-j and neutrino carriers. In thermal physics
A1's admissibility condition (Var(E) > 0) rejects the Schwarzschild and de Sitter thermal families outright, and D2 coincides with
thermodynamic length so that S is the excess length of a sub-optimal protocol. D8 turns critical slowing down into divergent
memory depth.
Where it is not: oscillators. Class (e) produced no SHARP row. The phase arc of a rotor is pi per half-turn by definition, so content
must be read from an observable whose metric the framework has to choose; the equal-half-turn-arcs claim fails on every
asymmetric cycle (FHN 0.945, biased Duffing 0.934) and holds on van der Pol only by symmetry; the cut placement on a
relaxation oscillator is an assignment, not a derivation. Classes (d) and (f) are almost entirely CONSIST: the framework's forms
coincide with Kalman, Cramér–Rao, Poisson and Omori but fix no constant.
Failures: the equanimity gain K(1)=1/phi is a random-walk result and drifts (0.60 to 0.50) as mean reversion strengthens; equal
arms is a symmetry, not a theorem. Open: the cost of a cut (Landauer) and the length L of a rotor's carrier.
Tension and proposed rewording: 'criticality = maximal openness, rho to 0' is true at a Hopf point and false at a second-order
thermal transition, where the Fisher metric diverges with the correlation length and rho to infinity. Minimal fix: state criticality
through D8 (memory depth d = 1/K(v) diverges as the relaxation rate vanishes), which holds for both, and confine the rho-to-0
statement to the Hopf case.
